aiOverview.content: Yes, the NASA Artemis II rocket launched successfully on Wednesday, April 1, 2026, at 6:35 p.m. EDT from Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The Space Launch System (SLS) propelled four astronauts toward the Moon, marking the first crewed mission to travel around it since 1972, with the crew now in Earth orbit. You can watch a replay of the Artemis II launch in this video:47sSpaceflight NowYouTube• Jun 19, 2025 47s Launch Details: The mission blasted off from Launch Pad 39B, with spectators in Florida seeing the rocket ascend. Mission Status: The four-astronaut crew (Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen) is currently conducting a 10-day mission. Next Steps: Following a successful orbital insertion, the crew will perform tests on the Orion capsule before embarking on a journey to orbit the Moon. The crew is safely in orbit, despite earlier minor technical concerns with the flight termination system that were resolved prior to lift-off.
